subject: Vendor proposals: warehouse + BI — review and ask list
messages:

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor proposals: warehouse + BI — initial packet

Folks,

I pulled together the vendor responses to our RFQ and attached the workbook (RFQ_DataWarehouse_2026.xlsx) with the line-item pricing we received. High level: Snowflake and BigQuery are both viable from a features perspective; Looker and Metabase cover the BI side but with different operational costs and embedding limits.

What I need from each of you by EOD Friday:
- Marcus: quick cost model (3-yr TCO) for Snowflake vs BigQuery using the attached pricing.csv tab.
- Monica: confirm whether the completed security questionnaire passes our baseline (especially egress/data residency notes).
- Connor: signal any migration blockers for moving Warehouses in Q4 (ETL, delta handling).

Also flagged a few commercial questions where we should push vendors: committed discount tiers, minimum consumption commitments, and storage split for retained exports. I circled these in the workbook.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Head of Procurement (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor proposals: warehouse + BI — initial packet

Lauren —

Quick take after running the numbers in the pricing tab:
- Snowflake, committed 36-mo with a 50% up-front commit gives us the best unit price for compute. If we can commit to the projected 18 months of steady traffic, we break even compared to BigQuery.
- BigQuery on-demand is cheaper for bursty ETL patterns; we'd pay more for sustained serving.
- Looker comes with higher up-front (implementation & modeling) costs; Metabase is much cheaper but will add ~0.5 FTE/year in admin/visualization support.

Open questions I left in the sheet: what discount band Snowflake will sign at public-sector pricing vs commercial; whether they will accept a step-down schedule (start smaller, scale to committed).

I recommend we ask Snowflake for a 12-mo ramped commit (25% -> 50% -> 100%) and hold off on a final decision until we validate with a short POC on our most expensive query classes.

—Marcus
Senior Analytics Engineer

Sarah —

Forwarding our internal summary. Can you confirm the following items by EOD Thursday:
1) Whether Snowflake will consider a ramped commit schedule over 12 months (25/50/100) and what that would mean for our unit price.
2) Details on data egress cost when we stream snapshots to our S3 backup; we left this blank in the RFQ.
3) Any add-on fees for cross-region replication (we have primary us-west and failover eu-west).

Attached: RFQ_DataWarehouse_2026.xlsx (pricing tab), procurement-price-breakdown-2026.csv

Best,
Lauren

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@snowflake.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor proposals: warehouse + BI — clarification on committed terms

Hi Lauren / Marcus,

Thanks for the packet and the clear questions. Short answers:
1) Ramped commit: yes, we can do a 12-mo step schedule (25/50/100) — price will be tiered: month 1-4 priced at the 25% band, 5-8 at the 50% band, 9-12 at the 100% band. We can provide a blended unit price for contract purposes; our commercial team typically guarantees no retroactive true-up if you meet the step targets.
2) Egress: streaming snapshots to S3 will incur standard egress rates; however, if you select a cross-region failover without active replication, you can reduce long-term costs. We can put storage for replicated failover under a negotiated storage allowance to offset some egress.
3) Cross-region replication: there is a small add-on for active replication between regions; passive failover has no ongoing charge beyond transfer/replication storage.

I'll follow up with a redlined SOW and a sample pricing schedule. If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call next week to walk the blended numbers.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Enterprise Solutions, Snowflake

Attachment: lookermetrics-proposal.pdf (sent for context; vendor partner references)

- For Looker (partner) the logging and audit export frequency is lower than our baseline; if we pick Looker we will ask for an API-based daily export instead of hourly.

Aside from those clarifications, the technical security posture reads well — no blocker on my side to proceed to commercial negotiation.

—Monica

Subject: Decision path and next steps: PO / POC / contract timeline

Thanks for the quick turn, team. Here are the actions I will take following this thread:
1) Schedule a 30-min sync with Sarah (Snowflake) next Tue to review the blended pricing and SOW.
2) Ask Looker for an amended logging SLA and a clearer implementation SOW for dashboard embedding (Rafael, please expect that ask).
3) Open a procurement PO request (deal DW-2026-Q3-001) for a 90-day POC with Snowflake — this will cover the initial commitment and allow us to validate the high-cost query patterns.
4) If POC passes, we will negotiate stepped commits (25/50/100) and lock a 36-mo discounted rate.

Connor — please list the minimal ETL datasets we need for the POC by Monday so procurement can size the contract. Marcus — I'll need your POC cost delta estimate by Monday as well. Monica — confirm the KMS key language for cross-region and we can include it in the SOW.

If nobody objects, I'll send the PO intake and book the vendor call.

Lauren
Head of Procurement (acting)
Redwood Inference
